site.sitedescription: Crystal Lagoon  is an open-water shallow lake (>1 m depth) on the south-eastern corner of Cape Barren Island. The lagoon is approximately 890 m in diameter and is constrained by 4–5 m high sand dunes (Fig. 1). Today the lagoon is surrounded by a mosaic of heathland, sedgeland, dense scrub, open forest and woodland. The woodlands are dominated by Eucalyptus nitida, while heathland and scrub are characterized by Acacia, Banksia, Allocasuarina, Kunzea, Leptospermum and Hakea species.  The lagoon margins are patchily occupied by a suite of shrubs including Allocasuarina monilifera, Banksia marginata, Kunzea ambigua, Leptospermum scoparium, Leptospermum laevigatum, Hakea sp., Acacia mucronata, Pultenea juniperina, Pomaderris, and Myoporum insulare, and wetland plants (Scirpus and Carex spp).
